draft.title: Atmospheric circulation and climate
card: The sun heats Earth unevenly. The tropics get more direct sunlight than the poles, so they receive more heat.
Warm air near the equator rises and leaves low pressure at the surface. Air sinks in other belts and makes high pressure there.
Wind is air moving from high pressure to low pressure. Winds and ocean currents carry heat and moisture around the world.
Together, the pressure belts, winds and ocean currents help set climate zones. Rising air tends to bring rain. Sinking air tends to bring dry weather, as in many of the world's deserts.
draft.remember: Uneven heating drives pressure belts and winds. With ocean currents, they help set climate zones.

a.q: What is the main reason winds blow across Earth's surface?
opts: Air moves from high pressure to low pressure
Air moves from low pressure to high pressure
Air moves from cool oceans to warm oceans
Air moves from the poles to the equator only
a.why: Uneven heating creates differences in air pressure, and air flows from high pressure towards low pressure. Moving from low to high pressure is the reverse of this.
a.clue: Think about where air starts and where it ends up.

b.q: A region has a belt of high pressure over it, with air sinking for most of the year. Which climate is it most likely to have?
opts: Dry, with little rain
Wet, with heavy rain
Cold, with frequent snow
Humid, with daily storms
b.why: Sinking air tends to bring dry weather, so regions under high pressure belts often have deserts. Wet climates are more likely where air rises, which is the opposite of this case.
b.clue: Does sinking air bring rain or dry weather?

a.best: Air moves from high pressure to low pressure

problems.detail: The clue 'Does sinking air bring rain or dry weather?' all but gives the answer away. It reduces the question to recalling a single word ('dry') rather than applying the idea.
